jurisdiction.name: Guatemala
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Guatemala has no AI law, AI strategy or data protection law. Its only official documents that steer AI are the Executive's Strategic Digital Transformation Plan, first published in 2025 and updated in June 2026, which makes an ethical National AI Strategy for the public sector a priority initiative and commits to a governance framework for emerging technologies; the strategy is being drafted with UNDP support. Data protection bills that would add rights over automated decisions and algorithmic transparency are pending in Congress.
lead_institutions: Comisión Nacional para la Modernización del Organismo Ejecutivo
Secretaría Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología (SENACYT)
narrative.review_notes: A follow-up review on 18 October 2026 reached the digital government commission and the Ministry of Public Finance, adding the 2025 edition of the digital transformation plan. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI material from the science secretariat and the banking superintendency. The national AI strategy and pending data protection bills are tracked as leads.

instruments.english_title: Strategic Plan for the Digital Transformation of the Executive Branch
instruments.issuing_authority: National Committee for the Modernization of the Executive Branch (Comité Nacional para la Modernización del Organismo Ejecutivo), Presidency of the Republic of Guatemala
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 dated June 2026 ('first updated version, 2026'), described as a living instrument subject to revision. It lists prioritised initiatives for 2025-2027, including drafting a National AI Strategy for the Executive Branch, which had not been published as of 2026-10-12.
instruments.summary: The Executive Branch's digital transformation plan, aligned with the General Government Policy 2024-2028 and coordinated by the National Committee for the Modernization of the Executive Branch, with the Presidential Commission for Open and Electronic Government (GAE) as the technical lead for implementation. Under its digital-government axis it makes a National Artificial Intelligence Strategy a prioritised 2025-2027 initiative to promote ethical, responsible and inclusive AI adoption in Executive Branch public services, with an ethical framework covering human dignity, data protection, non-discrimination and accountability. Its governance axis also calls for a governance framework setting principles for the ethical and transparent use of emerging technologies such as AI, blockchain and big data.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only official Guatemalan government document that commits to an AI strategy and AI ethics principles for the public sector; no AI-specific strategy or law exists yet.

instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Republic of Guatemala, Executive Branch (prepared by the Digital Transformation Working Group of the National Committee for the Modernization of the Executive Branch)
instruments.current_status: Earlier edition of the Executive Branch digital transformation plan, dated 2025 on its cover and published on the Ministry of Public Finance website. An updated edition (version 1.0, June 2026) was later published by the Presidency.
instruments.summary: The first published edition of the Executive Branch's digital transformation plan, prepared under the National Committee for the Modernization of the Executive Branch created by Acuerdo Gubernativo 106-2024. It sets out 35 digital initiatives across three central axes (digital government, digital economy, digital society) and four enabling axes, and prioritises for 2025-2027 a National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for the Executive Branch, with an ethical framework covering human dignity, data protection, non-discrimination and accountability. Its governance axis also proposes a governance framework setting principles for the ethical and transparent use of emerging technologies such as AI, blockchain and big data.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Earliest official Guatemalan government document committing to a national AI strategy and AI ethics principles for the public sector; kept for the timeline alongside the updated June 2026 edition.

organizations.name: National Committee for the Modernization of the Executive Branch
organizations.ai_governance_role: Created by Acuerdo Gubernativo 106-2024 to define the Executive Branch modernisation plan; coordinates the Strategic Plan for the Digital Transformation of the Executive Branch, which makes a National AI Strategy a prioritised initiative. Implementation is led technically by the Presidential Commission for Open and Electronic Government (GAE); the Secretaría Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología (SENACYT) was reported in 2026 to be drafting the AI strategy.

leads.title: Iniciativa 6464: Ley de Protección de Datos Personales y Garantía de Derechos Digitales
leads.english_title: Bill 6464: Personal Data Protection and Guarantee of Digital Rights Act
leads.issuing_authority: Congress of the Republic of Guatemala
leads.note: Pending bill (read 2026-10-12 at https://www.congreso.gob.gt/assets/uploads/info_legislativo/iniciativas/ceb66-6464.pdf; first reading noted by the plenary 5 December 2024). Includes a right to be informed about the use of algorithms in automated decisions and arts. 22-23 on the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions (incl. profiling) and to human intervention. Record as binding-law/data-privacy if enacted. Guatemala has no general data protection law or authority; other pending data protection bills: 6572 (noted 5 Aug 2025), 5811, 5940. Update 2026-10-18: not re-checked; status unchanged as far as known.

leads.title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (Organismo Ejecutivo)
leads.issuing_authority: Presidential Commission for Open and Electronic Government (GAE) / National Secretariat of Science and Technology (SENACYT)
leads.note: Prioritised initiative of the Strategic Plan for the Digital Transformation of the Executive Branch (June 2026). A UNDP-supported AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) started with GAE in October 2025; press reports in 2026 said SENACYT expected to finish a government AI strategy around late November/December 2026. No official text published as of 2026-10-12; record when published. Update 2026-10-18: the Presidential Commission for Open and Electronic Government website was searched ('inteligencia artificial', 'AILA'): only news items (AILA assessment, September 2025; regional AI dialogues); no strategy text published. SENACYT website still not accessible.
